```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5
)
library(reach.rate)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
```

**Audience:** technical. You maintain or extend the package: how the classes are built and how to add an accessor.

**Audience: maintainers and contributors.** If you use the package to fit
and apply ratings, you do not need this guide: read a rating through the
accessor functions (`rating_limbs()`, `rating_coefficients()`,
`rating_diagnostics()`, `rating_evidence()`, `rating_support()`,
`rating_bootstrap()`, `rating_history()` and `rating_provenance()`), which
are documented in the reference and used throughout the other vignettes.
This guide is for anyone changing the classes themselves, adding an
accessor, or writing a function that has to accept more than one
representation of a rating.

# Why S7 at all

[S7](https://rconsortium.github.io/S7/) is a typed object system for R,
built jointly by the R Consortium and Posit as a successor to S4 that
keeps S4's real guarantees (typed properties, validators that run on
construction) with a plainer syntax. What it buys the package is not
cosmetic: a `FlodeRating` cannot exist in a broken state, because its
validator runs before anyone gets to hold one.

Users never touch the properties directly. They go through accessors, so
where the package keeps something is free to change without breaking
their code. The properties are an implementation detail that maintainers
own, which is why this is the one place they are described.

# The class hierarchy

```{r hierarchy-diagram, echo=FALSE, fig.alt="Class hierarchy diagram: FlodeRatingBase (abstract) is the parent of FlodeRating and FlodeSegmentedRating; FlodeRatingTable stands separately", fig.height=4}
boxes <- data.table(
  class = c("FlodeRatingBase\n(abstract)", "FlodeRating", "FlodeSegmentedRating", "FlodeRatingTable"),
  x = c(1.8, 0.7, 2.9, 5.9), y = c(2, 0.7, 0.7, 1.35),
  w = c(2.2, 1.9, 2.3, 2.1), h = c(0.7, 0.7, 0.7, 0.7),
  fill = c("#cfd8dc", "#b3e5fc", "#b3e5fc", "#ffe0b2")
)
arrows <- data.table(
  x = c(0.7, 2.9), y = c(1.05, 1.05), xend = c(1.5, 2.2), yend = c(1.65, 1.65)
)

ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = boxes, aes(xmin = x - w / 2, xmax = x + w / 2, ymin = y - h / 2, ymax = y + h / 2, fill = fill), colour = "grey30") +
  geom_text(data = boxes, aes(x, y, label = class), size = 3.4, lineheight = 0.9) +
  geom_segment(data = arrows, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed"), colour = "grey30") +
  annotate("text", x = 5.9, y = 0.85, label = "separate -- not part of\nthe fit hierarchy", size = 3, colour = "grey40", lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.5, 7.2), ylim = c(0, 2.6)) +
  theme_void()
```

`FlodeRatingBase` is abstract: it is never constructed directly, and
exists to hold what `FlodeRating` (the result of `rate_optimise()`) and
`FlodeSegmentedRating` (the result of `rate_optimise_segmented()`) have in
common. `FlodeRatingTable` sits apart from that hierarchy entirely. It is
the equation-table representation that the gap-checking functions and
`apply_rating()` work with, not a fit in its own right, and it inherits
nothing from `FlodeRatingBase`.

Reading properties as a maintainer uses S7's functional form, which works
the same on every class:

```{r properties}
set.seed(1)
stage_m <- seq(0.3, 3, by = 0.1)
discharge_cms <- 5 * stage_m^1.5 * exp(rnorm(length(stage_m), sd = 0.03))
fit <- rate_optimise(discharge_cms, stage_m)

fit # each class has its own print method
class(fit) # the full inheritance chain, most-specific first
S7::prop_names(fit) # every property the class declares
S7::prop(fit, "limbs")[, .(limb, C, a, n)] # one property, by name
```

`print()` gives a one-line summary plus the coefficient table, in place of
R's default dump of every property. `class(fit)` shows the chain,
`reach.rate::FlodeRating`, `reach.rate::FlodeRatingBase`, `S7_object`,
confirming a `FlodeRating` is a `FlodeRatingBase` underneath.

The table below is what each class holds and which accessor exposes it.
When you add something to a class, add it here and to an accessor.

| Property | Held by | Exposed by |
|---|---|---|
| per-limb bounds and equation | `FlodeRating`, `FlodeRatingTable` | `rating_limbs()` |
| per-limb diagnostics and uncertainty | `FlodeRating` | `rating_diagnostics()`, `rating_coefficients()` |
| joint coefficients | `FlodeSegmentedRating` | `rating_coefficients()` |
| evidence (a `FlodeEvidence`: stable `evidence_id`, source, inclusion, weight) | `FlodeRating`, `FlodeSegmentedRating` | `rating_evidence()`, `rating_support()` |
| bootstrap draws | `FlodeRating` | `rating_bootstrap()` |
| `fit_origin`, `lifecycle` and previous version | all three | `rating_history()` |
| `schema_version` | all three | `rating_provenance()` |
| provenance | `FlodeRating`, `FlodeSegmentedRating` | `rating_provenance()` |
| per-attempt multi-start record | `FlodeRating`, `FlodeSegmentedRating` | summarised in `rating_diagnostics()` |

# Validators: what you cannot accidentally build

Constructing one of these classes with something structurally wrong fails
immediately, with a specific error, rather than producing an object that
only breaks later when some downstream function trips over the missing
piece.

```{r validator-demo, error=TRUE}
FlodeRating(
  limbs = data.table(limb = 1, C = 1, a = 0, n = 1), # missing lower_stage_m/upper_stage_m
  gaugings = data.table(discharge_cms = 1, stage_m = 1)
)
```

That error fires at construction time and names exactly which columns are
missing, not three functions later as an obscure `NULL`. Every exported
class validates its own structural requirements (required columns, `C` and
`n` positivity, contiguous limb bounds, and more) the same way. When you
add a property, add its validation in the same change.

# `S7_inherits()`: accepting either representation

Several exported functions (`plot_rating_cross_section()`,
`apply_rating_inverse()`, `graft_rating()` among them) accept either a
`FlodeRating` or a `FlodeRatingTable` and quietly bridge the former to the
latter internally. `S7_inherits()` is how they tell which one they were
handed, and it is the right check in your own code:

```{r s7-inherits-demo}
S7::S7_inherits(fit, FlodeRating)
S7::S7_inherits(fit, FlodeRatingBase) # also TRUE: FlodeRating IS a FlodeRatingBase

rating_dt <- data.table(lower_level = 0, upper_level = 3, C = 5, a = 0, n = 1.5)
tbl <- FlodeRatingTable(table = rating_dt)
S7::S7_inherits(tbl, FlodeRating) # FALSE: a table is not a fit

accept_either <- function(x) {
  if (S7::S7_inherits(x, FlodeRating)) "got a fit" else if (S7::S7_inherits(x, FlodeRatingTable)) "got a table" else stop("neither")
}
accept_either(fit)
accept_either(tbl)
```

`inherits(x, "FlodeRating")` does *not* work reliably, because S7 classes
are namespace-qualified (`"reach.rate::FlodeRating"`, visible in the
`class(fit)` output above). `S7_inherits()` checks against the class
object itself, so there is no string to get wrong.

# The amendment chain

Every class carries how it came to be (`fit_origin`), where it stands in
review (`lifecycle`, which the package leaves at `"draft"`: approval is a
person's decision) and a link to the version it was amended from, so
amending a rating never silently loses what it was amended from.
Users read the whole chain with `rating_history()`:

```{r audit-chain}
rating_dt <- data.table(
  lower_level = c(0, 1.5), upper_level = c(1.5, 3),
  C = c(3, 5), a = c(0, 0.1), n = c(1.5, 1.6)
)
tbl <- FlodeRatingTable(table = rating_dt)
aligned <- align_limb_equations(tbl)

rating_history(aligned)
identical(S7::prop(S7::prop(aligned, "previous"), "table"), S7::prop(tbl, "table")) # the exact object it was built from
```

The previous version is not a copy or a re-derived approximation: it is
the literal pre-amendment object. Chain several amendments and the history
grows by one row each time, until the oldest row, the original
independently-fitted or independently-built starting point. This is what
the user guide means by "an audit trail by construction rather than by
discipline": there is no code path that produces an amended table with
nowhere to point its previous version at. Any new function that amends a
rating must set it.

# Shared generics: one name, dispatched by class

Several functions work identically whichever class you hold, because they
are S7 methods registered against shared generics, not separate functions
per class:

```{r shared-generics, eval=FALSE}
rating_plot(fit) # works on FlodeRating and FlodeSegmentedRating
apply_rating(fit, stage_dt) # FlodeRating, FlodeSegmentedRating, FlodeRatingTable
as_rating_table(fit) # converts a fit to FlodeRatingTable
rating_limbs(fit) # and the other accessors: see below
```

S7's method dispatch picks the registered implementation for whatever
class the object actually is. That is the payoff of the hierarchy: it is
what makes "call the same function regardless of representation" work.

# Adding an accessor

The accessors follow one pattern, so a new one should too.

1. **A generic with a method per class**, defined in `R/accessors.R`:
   `new_generic("rating_thing", "x")`, then one method for each of
   `FlodeRating`, `FlodeSegmentedRating` and `FlodeRatingTable` where the
   information exists, and a method for `class_any` that refuses anything
   that is not a rating.
2. **Say so where the class has nothing to give.** A class that does not
   hold the information raises an error that names the class, says why,
   and says what to use instead (see `.accessor_not_held()`), rather than
   returning an empty table that looks like an answer.
3. **Return a copy.** Changing the result must never change the rating.
4. **Unit-suffixed columns** (`_m`, `_cms`, `_pct`) in a `data.table`, or a
   documented list. Uncertainty that was not computed is `NA`, never zero.
5. **Document it on the generic's own block.** roxygen cannot name a call
   of the form `method(generic, Class) <- function(...)`, so documentation
   written above a method is silently dropped and never reaches the
   reference. This has already cost the package a missing example and the
   missing argument documentation for `apply_rating()`. Put the arguments,
   the return value and the examples on the generic, and mark a method's
   comment block as not for the reference (the no-Rd tag).
6. **Test it on every class**, for success and failure: the shape and
   values on a hand-built rating where the answer is known, the failure
   message for each class that cannot answer, and that the result is a
   copy.

Tests may read properties directly where they are testing the class
itself. Documentation, vignettes, examples and the README must not.
